headline: Federal Judge Orders Texas to Air Condition All State Prisons by 2029
meta_description: A federal judge has ruled that Texas must install air conditioning in every state prison by 2029, deciding extreme heat violates the Constitution.
summary_short: Formerly incarcerated advocates secured a landmark federal court victory requiring Texas to cool all state prisons within five years.
body:
A federal judge has ordered Texas to install air conditioning in every state prison by 2029, ruling that extreme heat in detention facilities violates the Constitution. The decision represents a major win for formerly incarcerated advocates who brought the case forward.

The ruling recognizes that subjecting incarcerated people to extreme temperatures constitutes cruel and unusual punishment. By setting a 2029 deadline, the court has given the state a concrete timeline to address conditions that have long posed serious health and safety risks to prisoners across Texas facilities.

This victory demonstrates the power of those with lived experience in the prison system using their voices to demand systemic change. The case highlights how legal action, grounded in constitutional protections, can drive real improvements in conditions for some of the most vulnerable people in America's criminal justice system.
quick_facts: Federal judge orders Texas to air condition all state prisons
Deadline set for 2029 to complete air conditioning installations
Formerly incarcerated advocates won the landmark case
Ruling: extreme heat violates the Constitution
